definition.title: Relativity Visualizations
definition.summary: Deterministic one-dimensional inertial-frame special-relativity teaching model.
assumptions: Frames S and S' are inertial, their x axes are aligned, and S' moves at constant +x velocity relative to S.
Proper time is measured by a clock for which the defining events occur at the same position.
Proper length is measured in the object's rest frame; contracted length uses simultaneous endpoint positions in the frame where the object moves.
The simultaneity pair is simultaneous in S with event B at non-negative x separation from event A.
The light-cone diagram uses reviewed normalized c=1 teaching coordinates rather than browser-computed physics.
limitations: No acceleration, non-inertial frames, twin-paradox turnaround dynamics, or rotating frames.
No relativistic velocity addition, Doppler shift, momentum, energy, four-vectors, or arbitrary three-dimensional boosts.
No general-relativity or gravitational-redshift calculation; the certified Schwarzschild lab owns that model.
Length contraction is a frame-dependent coordinate measurement, not a photographic rendering prediction.
The 0-0.99c speed range is a reviewed teaching/numerical product bound, not a physical applicability cutoff.

equations.meaning: Lorentz factor for relative speed v=beta*c.

sources.title: 5.3 Time Dilation — University Physics Volume 3
sources.record_reference: Proper time is measured where the two defining events occur at the same location; Delta_t=gamma*Delta_tau.

sources.title: 5.4 Length Contraction — University Physics Volume 3
sources.record_reference: Proper length is measured in the object's rest frame and moving-frame length is L=L0/gamma.

sources.title: 5.5 The Lorentz Transformation — University Physics Volume 3
sources.record_reference: t'=gamma*(t-vx/c^2); separated events simultaneous in one inertial frame need not be simultaneous in another.
sources.citation: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 3, §5.5 The Lorentz Transformation.
sources.claim_scope: Lorentz time transformation and relativity-of-simultaneity sign convention.

light_cone.coordinate_system: normalized ct-versus-x teaching coordinates with c=1
light_cone.note: The reviewed normalized lines are conceptual causal boundaries. The browser may render these fixed coordinates but must not derive them from user input.

validation_fixtures.purpose: Check beta=0.6 gives gamma=1.25, 10 s to 12.5 s, 100 m to 80 m, and one-light-second simultaneity offset -0.75 s.
Check beta=0 preserves proper time/length and produces zero simultaneity offset.
Check beta=0.99 remains finite throughout the reviewed domain.
Check gamma increases monotonically over representative increasing beta samples.
Check dilated coordinate time is never below proper time in the reviewed beta domain.
Check moving-frame length is never above proper length in the reviewed beta domain.
Check positive beta and positive +x separation produce a negative B-minus-A time offset in S'.
Check proper-time, proper-length, and event-separation outputs scale linearly when beta is fixed.
Reject booleans, non-finite values, and values outside public bounds.
Require repeated model evaluations to be value-identical.
Reject changed sources, constants, light-cone geometry, preset, validation identity, and duplicate JSON keys.

scientific_validation.method: Use the reviewed OpenStax Lorentz/time/length equations with exact NIST c, then test the exact beta=0.6 ratio case, identity and upper bounds, monotonic/order properties, fixed-beta scaling, sign convention, determinism, and strict artifact mutation rejection.
